Requirement: To realize VOR learning, it is necessary to integrate input [U.VN-input] head motion information (Output Semantics: head velocity and acceleration information), input [U.PN] visual motion information (Output Semantics: visual motion information optic flow), and input [U.IO] error signals (Output Semantics: teaching signals based on retinal slip error), and generate output [U.VN-output] adaptively modulated VOR motor commands (Output Semantics: adaptively modulated VOR motor commands). This transformation adaptively improves the compensation accuracy of eye movements for head motion based on visual feedback.
Requirement realization by interface: The Interface shows [U.VN-input], [U.PN], and [U.IO] as inputs and [U.VN-output] as output. Child node [R.multisensory-context-encoding] encodes multisensory context from vestibular and visual motion information, and [R.adaptive-sensory-motor-transformation] learns sensory-motor transformation based on error signals to generate adaptive motor commands, thereby realizing the Requirement.
Capability: Capability to integrate multisensory information (vestibular, visual) and error signals, and adaptively modulate sensory-motor transformation through supervised learning. The cerebellum functions as a supervised learning machine based on Marr-Albus-Ito theory, where error signals (climbing fibers) serve as teaching signals, sensory context (parallel fibers) as input patterns, and synaptic plasticity (LTD/LTP) as learning mechanism (Marr 1969; Albus 1971; Ito 2002). This capability enables adaptive adjustment of motor commands to environmental changes.
Mechanism: Multisensory context encoding encodes sensory patterns in high-dimensional representational space, and error-driven synaptic plasticity modulates weights at parallel fiber-Purkinje cell synapses. Based on modulated synaptic weights, Purkinje cells generate inhibitory signals to vestibular nuclei, changing VOR gain. Lateral inhibition refines output patterns, improving learning precision.

Requirement: To realize multisensory context encoding, it is necessary to integrate input [U.VN-input] head motion information and input [U.PN] visual motion information, and generate spatially distributed multisensory integrated information (Output Semantics: temporally and spatially filtered multisensory integrated information, spatially distributed information, lateral inhibition signals, inhibitory gain control signals) to outputs [U.PC], [U.BC], [U.SC], [U.GoC]. This transformation enables downstream Purkinje cells to receive diverse sensory conjunction patterns, enabling conjunctive learning.
Requirement realization by interface: The Interface shows [U.VN-input] and [U.PN] as inputs and [U.PC], [U.BC], [U.SC], [U.GoC] as outputs. Child node [R.sensory-integration-with-gain-control] executes sensory integration and inhibitory gain control, and [R.spatial-information-distribution] spatially distributes sparsified information, thereby realizing the Requirement.
Capability: Capability to integrate different sensory modalities, perform expansion recoding into high-dimensional representational space under inhibitory gain control, and spatially distribute. The granular layer embeds input patterns in high-dimensional space through approximately 100-fold expansion, and realizes pattern separation by sparsifying activity through Golgi cell inhibition (Cayco-Gajic et al. 2023; Gilmer & Person 2022). Through spatial distribution by parallel fibers, each Purkinje cell receives over 100000 different sensory conjunction patterns.
Mechanism: Granule cells randomly integrate multiple mossy fiber inputs (vestibular, visual), and Golgi cells provide feedforward and feedback inhibition to sparsify activity. Granule cell axons bifurcate in T-shape as parallel fibers, extending several millimeters in molecular layer to contact numerous Purkinje cells. This geometric arrangement enables broad spatial distribution of sensory information, enabling associative learning downstream.

Requirement: To realize adaptive sensory-motor transformation, it is necessary to integrate input [U.PF] multisensory integrated information (Output Semantics: spatially distributed multisensory integrated information) and input [U.IO] error signals (Output Semantics: VOR error signals), and generate output [U.VN-output] adaptively modulated VOR motor commands. This transformation learns sensory-motor mapping based on synaptic plasticity, and realizes VOR gain adjustment refined by lateral inhibition.
Requirement realization by interface: The Interface shows [U.PF] and [U.IO] as inputs and [U.VN-output] as output. Child node [R.error-driven-plasticity] induces synaptic plasticity based on error signals to learn sensory-motor transformation, and [R.lateral-inhibitory-refinement] refines output patterns through lateral inhibition, thereby realizing the Requirement.
Capability: Capability to adaptively modulate synaptic weights based on error signals, refine output through lateral inhibition, and learn sensory-motor transformation. Purkinje cells execute LTD/LTP at parallel fiber-Purkinje cell synapses, with complex spikes via climbing fibers functioning as teaching signals (Broussard & Titley 2013; Najafi et al. 2024). Lateral inhibition by basket and stellate cells realizes winner-take-all computation, improving spatial precision of output (Gao et al. 2019).
Mechanism: Coincident detection of parallel fiber activity and climbing fiber activity integrates calcium at IP3 receptors, activating PKC to execute AMPA receptor endocytosis (LTD) or insertion (LTP). Based on modulated synaptic weights, Purkinje cells generate inhibitory signals to vestibular nuclei. Basket cells inhibit around axon initial segment, and stellate cells inhibit dendrites, suppressing Purkinje cells peripheral to active parallel fiber beam and relatively enhancing central output.

Requirement: To realize sensory integration with gain control, it is necessary to integrate input [U.VN-input] head motion information and input [U.PN] visual motion information, and generate output [U.PF] temporally and spatially filtered multisensory integrated information. Granule cells ([U.GrC], Output Semantics: temporally and spatially filtered multisensory integrated information) execute sensory integration and expansion recoding, and Golgi cells ([U.GoC], Output Semantics: inhibitory gain control signals) realize pattern separation by sparsifying activity through inhibitory gain control.
Requirement realization by interface: The Interface shows [U.VN-input] and [U.PN] as inputs and [U.PF] as output. Child UC [U.GrC] integrates mossy fiber inputs, and [U.GoC] provides feedforward and feedback inhibition, thereby realizing the Requirement. Since [U.GrC] axons become [U.PF], the output is [U.PF].
Capability: Capability to integrate different sensory modalities and perform expansion recoding and pattern separation under inhibitory gain control. Each granule cell randomly integrates approximately 4 different mossy fiber inputs and embeds in high-dimensional space through approximately 100-fold expansion (Gilmer & Person 2022). Golgi cell inhibition acts through two mechanisms phasic (alpha1-GABA-A receptor) and tonic (alpha6-GABA-A receptor), with moderate inhibition levels optimizing pattern separation performance (D'Angelo et al. 2025).
Mechanism: Granule cells receive multiple mossy fiber inputs via dendritic claws and fire when simultaneous inputs exceed threshold. Golgi cells integrate excitatory inputs from mossy fibers (feedforward) and parallel fibers (feedback), executing GABAergic inhibition to granule cell dendrites within cerebellar glomeruli. This inhibition sparsifies granule cell population activity, limiting overlap between sensory ensembles. Timing of inhibition controls temporal fidelity of information transfer.

Requirement: To realize spatial information distribution, it is necessary to spatially distribute and transmit sparse multisensory integrated information from granule cells ([U.GrC]) generated from inputs [U.VN-input] and [U.PN] to outputs [U.PC], [U.BC], [U.SC], [U.GoC] via parallel fibers ([U.PF], Output Semantics: spatially distributed multisensory integrated information). This distribution enables each Purkinje cell to receive diverse sensory context information via approximately 100000 parallel fiber synapses, enabling conjunctive learning.
Requirement realization by interface: The Interface shows [U.VN-input] and [U.PN] as inputs and [U.PC], [U.BC], [U.SC], [U.GoC] as outputs. Child UC [U.GrC] generates sensory integrated information, and [U.PF] (GrC axons) spatially distributes that information to downstream UCs, thereby realizing the Requirement. The one-to-many structure of [U.PF] supports spatial distribution.
Capability: Capability to spatially distribute sparse information broadly and transmit high-dimensional information patterns. Each parallel fiber extends several millimeters in molecular layer, intersecting with numerous Purkinje cell dendrites along its trajectory. Each Purkinje cell receives synaptic inputs from over 100000 different parallel fibers, enabling representation of vast numbers of sensory conjunction patterns. This geometric arrangement provides foundation for cerebellum to function as kernel machine.
Mechanism: Granule cell axons ascend to molecular layer and bifurcate in T-shape to form parallel fibers. Each parallel fiber forms excitatory glutamatergic synapses on Purkinje cell, basket cell, stellate cell, and Golgi cell dendrites encountered along its trajectory. Synaptic transmission is mediated by AMPA receptors and mGlu1 receptors. Information from same granule cell simultaneously reaches multiple spatially separated downstream neurons, enabling parallel information processing.

Requirement: To realize error-driven plasticity, it is necessary to integrate input [U.PF] multisensory integrated information, input [U.IO] error signals, and inputs [U.BC] and [U.SC] lateral inhibition signals, and generate VOR inhibitory signals to output [U.VN-output]. Purkinje cells ([U.PC], Output Semantics: adaptively modulated VOR inhibitory signals through learning) induce LTD/LTP based on coincident detection of parallel fiber ([U.PF]) activity and climbing fiber ([U.IO]) activity, execute sensory-motor transformation with learned synaptic weights, and modulate VOR gain.
Requirement realization by interface: The Interface shows [U.PF], [U.IO], [U.BC], [U.SC] as inputs and [U.VN-output] as output. Child UC [U.PC] integrates massive excitatory inputs from parallel fibers, teaching signals from climbing fibers, and inhibitory modulation from basket/stellate cells, with coincident activation of [U.PF] and [U.IO] inducing synaptic plasticity, thereby realizing the Requirement.
Capability: Capability to integrate large-scale excitatory inputs, adaptively modulate synaptic weights based on error signals, and learn sensory-motor transformation under lateral inhibition. Purkinje cells execute LTD/LTP at parallel fiber-Purkinje cell synapses, with LTD mediating gain decrease and LTP mediating gain increase (Broussard & Titley 2013). Complex spikes via climbing fibers function as teaching signals, inducing Hebbian or anti-Hebbian plasticity for simultaneous activation patterns of parallel fibers (Najafi et al. 2024).
Mechanism: mGluR1 activation and IP3 generation by parallel fiber stimulation, and voltage-gated calcium channel opening and calcium influx by climbing fiber stimulation are integrated at IP3 receptors. This coincident detection activates PKC, phosphorylating AMPA receptors causing their removal by endocytosis producing LTD (Ito 2002). High-frequency parallel fiber stimulation induces LTP increasing AMPA receptors. Based on modulated synaptic weights, Purkinje cells provide GABAergic inhibitory projections to vestibular nuclei, with changes in inhibition strength modulating VOR gain.

Requirement: To realize lateral inhibitory refinement, it is necessary to detect spatial activity patterns of input [U.PF] and provide inhibition to output [U.PC] to sharpen Purkinje cell output patterns. Basket cells ([U.BC], Output Semantics: lateral inhibition signals that sharpen output patterns) inhibit around axon initial segment, and stellate cells ([U.SC], Output Semantics: lateral inhibition signals that modulate dendritic information integration) inhibit dendrites, improving spatial contrast of output through winner-take-all computation.
Requirement realization by interface: The Interface shows [U.PF] as input and [U.PC] as output. Child UCs [U.BC] and [U.SC] receive excitatory input from parallel fibers and provide GABAergic inhibition to Purkinje cells, thereby realizing the Requirement. Inhibition to different target sites axon initial segment (BC) and dendrites (SC) enables multilayer modulation of input-output.
Capability: Capability to detect parallel fiber activity patterns and refine Purkinje cell output through feedforward lateral inhibition. Basket cells are excited along trajectory of activated parallel fibers and provide strong GABAergic inhibition to axon initial segments of nearby Purkinje cells, realizing winner-take-all computation. Stellate cells provide inhibition to dendrites, locally modulating dendritic information integration. These inhibitions complexly shape neuronal response dynamics rather than simple blocking (Gao et al. 2019).
Mechanism: Basket cell axons extend transversely across folium, forming basket-like synaptic contacts around axon initial segments of multiple Purkinje cells and releasing GABA to powerfully suppress action potential generation. Stellate cell axons form GABAergic synapses on Purkinje cell dendrites providing local inhibition. Purkinje cells located on both sides of active parallel fiber beam are selectively suppressed, relatively enhancing output of centrally activated Purkinje cells. Basket cells control output and stellate cells control input integration, realizing multilayer modulation.
